name: game-editor
description: Work on the Godot 4 project open in your editor, with guards and an approval per plan that says what is lost, and put GameForge sprite sheets, tile sets (a level map becomes its dual-grid tilemap), sound effects and music loops straight into the open scene. Through Godot AI (hi-godot/godot-ai) 4.3.0. Reads never run a @tool script, decided the way Godot decides it. plan_change writes nothing and returns the whole plan with each value now and after and what Godot AI does inside each step; apply_plan runs only the newest plan and reads each step back. A plan that deletes, overwrites, discards unsaved work or runs code it wrote asks a second time with confirm_risky_plan, after a list of what is lost. Play findings carry file:line and evidence, and GameForge's playtest report becomes the same fix steps. A headless play writes res://ge_headless_arm.gd and .tscn, then removes them; project.godot is not left changed. Studio scores one sentence with a headless Godot exit code. A loop that prints STUDIO and quits 0 is not a pass. The running root has to be the loop.gd this package wrote, so another script on that scene is not a pass. An autoload in project.godot or override.cfg is unverified script: and Godot is not started. When the extra script is an embedded GDScript on the scene, the inspection process starts and that extra script does not run. The verdict uses --path on a directory this process creates, and that directory does not contain override.cfg. A pass needs check.gd unchanged and, when the sentence names timeout_lose or restart, physics_frames of at least the sentence's seconds times 60. A 0.05 second timer is not that timeout. A loop.gd passes only when its bytes are the script this process writes for that sentence. Any other text on the var limit_seconds line is unverified script: res://studio/loop.gd, Godot is not started for that byte-different loop.gd, and the sha256 record is not the allow-list. The check watches the key become a child of the player, not the loop's flags. Godot runs with --fixed-fps 60. timeout_lose is the fresh round's physics frames, the sentence's seconds times 60, so 60 seconds is 3600 frames, while Engine.time_scale stays 1 and the physics tick rate stays 60. The Limit timeout signal is not a pass. If Limit stops before those frames, the exit code is not 0. restart is true only after those frames, when the key is back on the floor, the door collision is back, and the player is back at the start position with velocity near zero. The scene hash covers the scene and the script. After a trusted exit 0, studio can download the pinned Godot 4.7.2 export template and serve the Web build on 127.0.0.1.
